body: Reflexivity: participants' beliefs change the fundamentals they are trying to price. Typical boom-bust sequence (Soros, Alchemy of Finance): (1) an unrecognised trend begins; (2) a prevailing bias forms and reinforces it - rising prices ease financing (equity issuance, collateral-backed credit), which lifts reported growth; (3) tests survive, conviction grows; (4) a divergence opens between belief and reality; (5) a twilight period where the trend continues on momentum but doubts grow; (6) a crossover and accelerating reversal. Indian examples: 2003-08 infra/realty (rising land values -> bigger loans -> more projects -> higher valuations -> QIPs), 2023-24 PSU rerating (rising prices -> retail and MF inflows -> more buying), 2024 SME IPOs (oversubscription -> listing gains -> more applicants). Rules for individuals: identify the feedback loop and its fuel (credit, IPO funding, retail flows); ride early only with small size; watch the fuel - when financing tightens (RBI/SEBI action, funding costs, lock-up expiries, promoter selling) the loop breaks. Risk: timing is hard; many 'bubbles' run far longer than expected.
title: Soros: reflexivity and boom-bust sequences
